deep.reconstruction:
This page is a reading excerpt, not original research. It continues Riemann's notebook of journal excerpts on natural philosophy. The neighbouring pages cover Chebyshev-type bounds for psi(x) before and Wilson's pyrometer and Pasteur's work on hemihedry after.

Bibliographic entries:
(a) Poggendorff's Annalen LXXXVII.2: 'Über den Zusammenhang der Lehre vom Diamagnetismus mit der Lehre von dem Magnetismus und der Elektricität'. This title matches W. Weber's paper, Pogg. Ann. 87 (1852), as far as I recall. Riemann gives only the title.
(b) Dingler's Polytechnisches Journal CXXV.6: M. H. Jacobi, 'Über die Theorie der elektromagnetischen Maschinen'. This is an abstract by Dr. H. Hammer of Jacobi's memoir in the Bulletin de la Classe physico-mathématique of the St. Petersburg Academy, T. IX, Nos. 19-20.

Riemann quotes Jacobi's description of the machine. Its parts are insulated wire coils with or without soft-iron cores, arranged as a moving and a fixed system. A commutator reverses or breaks the current whenever the poles meet. A galvanic battery drives it. Whether the motion is rotary or oscillating is irrelevant.

The geometry is held fixed. The free variables are:
- the battery's electromotive force (k per cell, n cells);
- the number of windings beta (taken equal in the moving and fixed electromagnets);
- the total resistance rho;
- the speed v, which is set by the mechanical load.

For the machine held at rest:
1) i = n k / rho (Ohm's law, as written).
2) Zinc consumed per unit time: q = n i = n^2 k / rho (Faraday: each of the n cells dissolves zinc in proportion to i).
3) Magnetism of each electromagnet system: m = beta i = beta n k / rho (Lenz-Jacobi law: magnetism proportional to ampere-turns).
4) Mutual attraction: mu = m^2 = beta^2 n^2 k^2 / rho^2.

Quantities at speed v carry primes. Motion induces a magneto-electric counter-current:
(5) i_1 = i - i'.
(6) i_1 is proportional to m', beta and v and inversely to rho, so i_1 = kappa m' beta v / rho = kappa beta^2 i' v / rho.

Here kappa is independent of these quantities. For a given shape it depends on the coercive force of the electromagnets and only slightly on the coil resistance. Jacobi takes kappa as the measure of coercive force.

Implicit step (mine; it is stated on the next page): from i - i' = kappa beta^2 i' v / rho one gets
- i' = n k / (rho + kappa beta^2 v),
- m' = beta n k / (rho + kappa beta^2 v).

The next page continues:
- Load R = mu' = m'^2.
- Useful work J = R v = v (beta n k)^2 / (rho + kappa beta^2 v)^2 = (beta n k sqrt(R) - R rho) / (kappa beta^2).
- The maximum is at R_0 = beta^2 n^2 k^2 / (4 rho^2), i.e. v_0 = rho / (kappa beta^2), with J_0 = n^2 k^2 / (4 rho kappa).
- Then q_0' = n^2 k / (2 rho) and the duty is epsilon = J_0 / q_0' = k / (2 kappa).

The purpose is Jacobi's optimisation of the efficiency of electric motors, essentially the maximum-power-transfer result: at maximum work the current falls to half its standstill value.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. Formulas 1)-6) are internally consistent: m' = beta i' turns kappa m' beta v / rho into kappa beta^2 i' v / rho.
Physically, eq. 2) treats zinc consumption as n times the current, i.e. it counts all n cells. This is Jacobi's convention, not a slip.
Treating mu = m^2 as the force (the product of two equal magnetisms) is Jacobi's idealisation of the Lenz-Jacobi law. It ignores saturation, which Jacobi himself acknowledged.

results.what: Current, zinc consumption and electromagnet strength at standstill: i = nk/rho, q = n^2 k/rho, m = beta i, mu = m^2
results.modern_name: Ohm's law, Faraday's electrolytic law, Lenz-Jacobi law (magnetisation proportional to ampere-turns)

results.what: Back-EMF (counter-current) proportional to speed, magnetism and turns: i_1 = kappa beta^2 i' v / rho
results.modern_name: Back-EMF of a DC motor (induced counter-EMF proportional to speed and flux)
results.usually_credited_to: M. H. Jacobi (1850-51), building on Lenz

results.what: Optimisation of the motor's useful work and duty (continued on the next page): J_0 = n^2 k^2/(4 rho kappa), epsilon = k/(2 kappa)
results.modern_name: Jacobi's maximum power theorem (maximum power transfer)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a faithful reading excerpt of Jacobi's published theory of electromagnetic engines from Dingler's Polytechnisches Journal, plus a bibliographic note on Weber's paper on diamagnetism. It is useful only as evidence of Riemann's reading in electromagnetism around 1852; there is no original content.

checkable.sympy: n,k,rho,kappa,beta,v=symbols('n k rho kappa beta v',positive=True); ip=symbols('ip'); simplify(solve(Eq(n*k/rho-ip, kappa*beta**2*ip*v/rho), ip)[0] - n*k/(rho+kappa*beta**2*v))
checkable.asserts: The counter-current equation (5)-(6) gives i' = nk/(rho+kappa beta^2 v); result 0.
Maximum useful work occurs at v0 = rho/(kappa*beta**2).
The maximum work is J0 = n^2 k^2/(4 rho kappa), independent of beta; result 0.
The duty is epsilon = J0/q0' = k/(2 kappa), with q0' = n i0' = n^2 k/(2 rho); result 0.
Two equivalent forms of the useful work, R v = (beta n k sqrt(R) - R rho)/(kappa beta^2); result 0.

transcription_corrections: Header year: the Annalen volume LXXXVII appeared in 1852, so '1850.10' may be a misreading of '1852' (or the digit is ambiguous in the image).
'den Stärkezustand der Magnetismus' should probably read 'den Stärkegrad des Magnetismus' or similar, i.e. the strength of magnetism.

The kappa sentence likely reads: 'kappa von diesen Grössen unabhängig ist und nur noch abhängt von der Coercitivkraft der Elektromagnete, wenn ihre Gestalt gegeben ist, und in geringem Maße vom Widerstand der Spirale'.
'(wo der Einfachheit wegen beyde gleich annimmt)' should probably read '(welche der Einfachheit wegen gleich angenommen)': the windings in the moving and fixed systems are taken as equal.
'Es bildet nun' should probably read 'Es bildet sich nun', i.e. a magneto-electric counter-current arises during the motion.
'untersucht die Werthe' should probably read 'unterscheidet die Werthe dieser Grössen bei der Geschwindigkeit v der Maschine durch Accente', i.e. primes mark the values at speed v.
